source_notes: United Kingdom equipment ladder, epochs 1-7 (1950-59, 60-69, 70-79, 80-89, 90-2004, 2005-15, 2016-). Written from recalled open-source figures (Janes-style references, official MoD figures) without web access; every uncertain field is listed in estimated_fields and confidence is per entry. Conventions: entered_service places the system in its epoch slot; later epochs carry either an upgrade entry or an {inherited_from_epoch} stub meaning 'same system, still in service'; a cell the UK never filled is {"designation": null} with a note -- absence is data. Ground vehicles use road_range_km; aircraft use combat_radius_km/ferry_range_km; ships use range_km at cruise and speed_kmh from max knots. gun_gen follows docs/11 section 2.1 (G1 20-pdr era ... G5 L/55A1 era); radar_gen follows the R-ladder (R1 early pulse ... R5 AESA/LPI). Roles gated to later epochs by docs/12 (ssn e2, ssbn e3, attack_helicopter e3, multirole e4, air_defence_destroyer e4) start at their gate epoch, except where the UK genuinely fielded the thing earlier -- those early entries are kept with a note so the designer can decide. Faction identity per docs/08: best area-air-defence radar (Sampson/Type 45), the only modern rifled gun with HESH (L11/L30), Chobham originated here, helicopter AEW as the carrier compromise, excellent ASW (SSNs, towed arrays, ASW helicopters), dedicated fleet auxiliaries. Deliberate absences that define the faction: no SPAAG ever (skipped guns for Rapier), no corvettes or missile boats (RN disbanded coastal forces 1957), no strategic bomber after 1984, no land long-range SAM after Bloodhound retired 1991, all-nuclear submarine force after 1994.
